problem: Existing VLN agents trained on residential scenes and basic instructions degrade in out-of-distribution (OOD) environments and with varied instruction styles (GSA-VLN). Prior dual-system (fast/slow) methods run the two systems in parallel, so slow-reasoning experience is never consolidated into the fast policy, and GR-DUET adapts only visually and ignores instruction style.
motivation: Real-world agents meet unseen building types and user-specific language, and a policy that stays fixed has spurious reasoning and cannot recognize its limits. Humans use System 1 for familiar cases and System 2 to reflect and internalize experience for later fast decisions; the paper mimics this loop.
key_idea: Couple a fast DUET policy with a slow LLM reflector that distills navigation logs into a structured experience library, which is retrieved and fused into the policy's visual features by attention, plus LLM-based instruction style conversion.
insight: The ablation shows the fast-slow framework (FSR) improves all splits (e.g. Test-N-Basic SR 53.7 to 58.4), while instruction style conversion (ISC) only helps Scene-style instructions (Test-N-Scene 47.9 to 50.4 when combined with FSR). Experience library capacity matters: K=20 is too small, K=200 hurts (redundancy interferes with attention fusion), with best results around 50-100. Caveat: the ablation baseline row (64.0 SR on Test-R-Basic) differs from the DUET baseline in the main tables, and the case study is a single hand-narrated example.
method: Fast reasoning: DUET-style topological-map policy (coarse/fine encoders, dynamic fusion) with CLIP-ViT-B/16 features; logs per-step history (viewpoint, local topology, action, step metrics) plus a Llama3.2-vision text description of each node view.
Experience structure: each experience E=[scene type, spatial context, spatial rules, navigation strategy, historical success rate, frequency], stored in a library of capacity K.

Slow reasoning: Llama3.2-vision, given a four-part CoT reflection prompt (intro, context, task decomposition, output format), analyzes logs of successes and failures and outputs structured experiences.

Experience retrieval and encoding: key features (scene type, context, strategy) are matched by similarity with a threshold, the top-M experiences are selected, and an embedding layer plus linear layer with activation maps each to a d-dim vector.

Experience fusion: multi-head attention with visual features as queries and experiences as keys/values, concatenation with the visual features, and a linear layer replace the original visual features fed into the policy.
Instruction style conversion: an LLM with a CoT prompt rewrites Scene/User-style instructions into Basic style, applied only if a confidence score exceeds a threshold.

setting.backbone: DUET policy (trained) + Llama3.2-vision (slow reasoning, image captioning, instruction conversion)
setting.training_data: GSA-R2R training data (residential scenes, from HM3D and MP3D), as in GR-DUET; the paper mentions no extra data. The LLM is used off-the-shelf.
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB views with GPS location and topological map; visual text descriptions from Llama3.2-vision
setting.action_space: Discrete navigable viewpoints on a topological nav-graph plus stop

numbers_note: Test-R-Basic and Test-N-Basic split names are from GSA-R2R (test split). Ablation tables (Tables 4-5) report a different baseline and K sweeps; they are not listed as separate entries. Table 2 (user styles) reports only SR/SPL.
results: Slow4Fast-VLN beats the previous best GR-DUET on GSA-R2R: SR 70.8 vs 69.3 on Test-R-Basic (+1.5) and 58.4 vs 56.6 on Test-N-Basic (+1.8; text says +2.2). On Scene instructions SR is 50.7 vs 48.1, and it wins most user-style columns (e.g. Keith 68.3 vs 66.7), though GR-DUET has a higher SPL on Moira (56.2 vs 55.4).
limitations: Gains over GR-DUET are modest (about 1.5-2.6 SR) and the paper reports no significance testing; the slow module relies on an LLM (Llama3.2-vision), which adds latency and dependence on prompts, though timing costs are not analyzed.

Experience library capacity K needs tuning per scene complexity (50 vs 100), and experiences are distilled from the test-time episodes' logs with no clear description of how ground-truth success signals are used.
Evaluated only in simulation on one benchmark (GSA-R2R); qualitative evidence is a single case study.
